title: Fluorite superionics: transition, activation energies and cell-size effects

decision_points.fork: Time base of the MSD tables: the lag column counts saved frames, and the frame interval (timestep x dump interval) must be read from each run's input deck
decision_points.wrong_choice: Assume one frame interval (0.04 ps, as in the CaF2/PbF2/AgI decks) for every material
decision_points.consequence: UO2 uses a 2 fs timestep (0.02 ps frames); all UO2 diffusion coefficients come out halved (-0.24 to -0.30 dex)

decision_points.fork: Which supercell to spend the budget on for T_c, activation energies and predictions (cost grows with atom count)
decision_points.wrong_choice: Use (or scan with) the cheap 96-atom cells
decision_points.consequence: c_V peak 140-570 K too high; 96-atom cells show one intermediate (CaF2 1.2/1.1 eV) or inverted (PbF2 0.22/0.42 eV) slope instead of the ordered/superionic change; predictions off by 0.19-0.32 dex

decision_points.fork: Whether the 768-atom cell is converged: it agrees with 1500 atoms above T_c but not in the ordered regime
decision_points.wrong_choice: Check convergence only where it is cheap or high-T and use the 768-atom value for the 4116-atom PbF2 runs
decision_points.consequence: PbF2 at 600 K: 768 atoms give D = 0.0088 vs 0.0170 A^2/ps for 4116 atoms (-0.29 dex)

decision_points.fork: Model for the size dependence: hydrodynamic Yeh-Hummer 1/L correction vs saturation once the collective disorder is captured
decision_points.wrong_choice: Fit D(L) = D_inf - k/L to the 96/324/768-atom cells and extrapolate
decision_points.consequence: At 600 K D(L) is non-monotonic (96 atoms highest) and the extrapolation to 4116 atoms is negative

decision_points.fork: One Arrhenius law across the transition vs separate ordered and superionic regimes
decision_points.wrong_choice: Single Arrhenius fit over all diffusive 768-atom temperatures
decision_points.consequence: CaF2 E_a = 1.42 eV for both regimes instead of 1.88 and 0.68 eV

decision_points.kind: regime judgement (transfer of a convergence conclusion)
decision_points.fork: Whether the 324-atom cell, adequate for CaF2/PbF2 T_c (within ~30 K of 768 atoms), is adequate for UO2
decision_points.consequence: UO2 c_V peak at 2940 K instead of 2743 K; UO2 2450 K prediction -0.22 dex

decision_points.fork: Type-I alpha-AgI vs type-II fluorites: whether the fluorite finite-size behaviour transfers
decision_points.wrong_choice: Correct small-cell AgI values by the fluorite large/small-cell ratio (x1.9)
decision_points.consequence: AgI predictions +0.23 to +0.25 dex; AgI D is size-independent from 32 to 864 atoms

graded_fields: transition_temperature_K (CaF2, PbF2, UO2; 768-atom c_V maximum) within 120 K
activation_energy_eV CaF2 ordered/superionic within 0.25 eV; PbF2 ordered within 0.15 eV, superionic within 0.10 eV
diffusion_predictions_A2_per_ps for 7 withheld runs, each within 0.15 dex
runtime_dependencies: numpy (runtime image); no extra lab dependencies

data_provenance.not_used: all *_heat folders and UO2_heat.zip (sibling task superionic-heat-transport-size-onsager)

notes: Design adaptations: thermodynamic-limit T_c is not graded (three sizes; 1/L vs 1/N extrapolations differ by >100 K), the graded T_c is that of the 768-atom cell. UO2 activation energies are not graded (ln D is curved; defensible windows give 3.4-5.1 eV ordered and 1.0-2.5 eV superionic). The "weak finite-size material" bit is a rubric item; AgI enters the grade through two 864-atom predictions. Block-averaging is served (SEMs), so noise-vs-signal is a rubric item; difficulty comes instead from the UO2 time base (deck metadata), the 768-atom convergence that holds above T_c but not below (PbF2 1500-atom runs), the 324-atom cell that is adequate for CaF2/PbF2 but not UO2, and the sign change of the size effect with temperature.

Ea_PbF2_ordered_eV.note: single Arrhenius (0.485) passes here; dp5 is caught by CaF2
